extracted.intended_audience: prospective middle-grades mathematics teacher candidates, teacher educators, and program administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and program standards describing university-level middle grades mathematics teacher preparation: certification requirements, course requirements and learning objectives, program assessment, and pedagogical/assessment practices used in preparing candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopted standards for candidate assessment (GSTEP & AMLE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Georgia Systematic Teacher Education Program (GSTEP) Framework for Accomplished Teaching and Association for Middle Level Education (AMLE) standards for Initial Middle Level Teacher Preparation are used to assess teacher candidates as they progress through the middle grades program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These frameworks are used as the program standards; candidates must satisfy each standard as determined by JHL COE Middle Grades faculty. GSTEP/NMSA standards are closely aligned with INTASC principles but provide detailed descriptions of knowledge, dispositions, and performances expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Areas of candidate assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates are assessed in areas of student development (particularly young adolescent); learning environments/philosophy and school organization; curriculum, instruction, and assessment; family and community involvement; and professional roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment covers knowledge, dispositions, and performances across these domains; faculty determine satisfaction of each standard before recommendation for certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: State certification exam requirement (GACE II / equivalent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students who successfully meet all assessed areas and pass the Georgia Certification Exam (GACE II) in their area of concentration are recommended to the State for middle grades certification (grades 4–8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early childhood program completers pass the GACE II exam specific to early childhood for recommendation in grades preK–5. Passing the appropriate state exam is a gate for recommendation to certification authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-level mathematics education goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematics education courses aim to provide students with a profound understanding of fundamental mathematics, knowledge of how students learn mathematics, and exposure to a variety of student-centered teaching strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses should include problem solving on meaningful problems, exploration using manipulatives and technology, written and oral mathematical communication, focus on conceptual 'why' rather than mere procedures, reading current research, and interdisciplinary integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course assessment formats and student experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses include diverse experiences: applying problem solving skills to meaningful problems, exploring mathematics with manipulatives/technology, communicating mathematically through written work and presentations, and field-based experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical assessments include final projects (lesson plans tied to middle school), presentations, oral exams, and opportunities to practice teaching; these are used to evaluate both content mastery and pedagogical skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: middle school teachers need specialized content and pedagogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Middle school mathematics teachers must have advanced content knowledge specific to the grades they will teach and be able to connect topics to the middle school classroom using appropriate pedagogical techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content courses for mathematics majors may not suffice; courses should be designed to develop mathematical maturity while explicitly connecting material to middle school curriculum and modeling pedagogy appropriate for young adolescents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-service mathematics course requirement (WOU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-service students seeking elementary/middle authorization with a mathematics focus are required to take six mathematics courses taught by the Mathematics Department: a core of five courses (Foundations I–III, Elementary Problem Solving, College Algebra for Elementary and Middle School Teachers) plus a sixth 300/400-level course from a specified list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard College Algebra may be substituted in some cases; students pursuing the math focus are required to take all ten courses listed for full focus programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-service / MS in Education mathematics requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Students pursuing a Master of Science in Education with mathematics as the content area are required to take 18 credits of mathematics and ED 637: Advanced Content Pedagogy–Mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some districts may grant professional development credits that apply toward the 18 credit requirement. Courses at the 500-level have graduate expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-numbered course graduate expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: In dual-numbered courses (undergraduate/graduate), graduate students have additional requirements: extra assignments, additional lesson plans in the final project, a more extensive presentation requirement, and more difficult/additional exam questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graduate-level work increases depth and rigor of assignments and assessments; instructors should specify graduate extensions in syllabi and coursepacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher Education Program entry requirements (WOU)
rubrics_metrics.description: To enter the Teacher Education Program, students must fulfill requirements including 41 credits in education (including two mathematics pedagogy courses), two letters of recommendation documenting supervised experience with children within the prior three years, and passing scores on specified examinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are expected to finish most coursework before entering the program; exceptions exist for course timing due to student-teaching schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required examinations for entry and endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must have passing scores for NES EAS (Reading, Writing, Mathematics) or accepted equivalents (Praxis I, CBEST, West-B) and ORELA Protecting Student and Civil Rights; additionally, a passing score on the NES Middle School Mathematics test is required before beginning Term Two.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing the NES Middle School Mathematics test is needed to add a Middle School Mathematics Endorsement in Oregon; comparable out-of-state Praxis scores may be used to satisfy federal 'highly qualified' definitions or for waivers if academic preparation meets state minimums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on out-of-state test equivalency and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: If an out-of-state teacher has passed Praxis: Middle School Mathematics, those scores may be used to satisfy federal 'highly qualified teacher' definitions; out-of-state teachers with a mathematics endorsement may be eligible for waiver of the NES Middle School Mathematics test if they meet Oregon's minimum academic preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program and state policies allow some portability/waiver subject to meeting state-defined academic preparation; candidates should consult state education department guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program evaluation metrics and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program quality can be assessed by job placement/retention, outside evaluations (e.g., accreditation, awards, recognitions), and alignment with research-based guidelines; however, job statistics may be a poor measure during weak economies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reliable indicators include continuous accreditation (NCATE/TSPC), recognition by organizations (NCTQ, AASCU awards), and documented alignment of coursework with research recommendations on teacher mathematical knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course pedagogy expectations (WOU)
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses for middle school teachers are taught in cooperative-group, exploratory learning environments where students present work regularly; guided discovery and opportunities to practice teaching build confidence and communication skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of manipulatives, technology, group work, presentations, and final projects that produce lesson plans are recommended pedagogical practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 392 / MTH 489: Algebra for Teachers — learning and practice with manipulatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize modeling integer operations and algebraic patterns using algebra tiles and algebra pieces; explore graphs and equations of absolute value and quadratic functions; use manipulatives to find key features and derive quadratic solution methods (completing the square).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After hands-on exploration, students discuss standard solution techniques without manipulatives. Course materials include Visual Algebra activity book and coursepack.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 491: Historical Topics — using history to inform teaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey historical development of arithmetic, algebra, and informal geometry with emphasis on topics and texts that provide historical context for classroom lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use historical texts (e.g., Historical Connections in Mathematics) to create lessons that connect mathematical ideas to their historical development for middle school audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 492: Abstract Algebra for Middle School Teachers — conceptual properties and classroom applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore properties of number sets and elementary group theory (commutativity, associativity, closure, identity, inverse) with applications to middle school topics such as cryptography and math art (Cayley tables).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use familiar operations on whole numbers, integers, rationals, reals as examples/non-examples; construct classroom activities (secret codes, art posters) to connect abstract concepts to student experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 493: Experimental Probability & Statistics — practical data literacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop insights into probability and statistics emphasizing data types, data collection/sampling, bias, displays and interpretation, measures of center/variability, correlation vs causation, elementary probability, and the Central Limit Theorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach with real-life data and simulations; about 40% of the class uses computer applications (Excel) for large data analysis, graphing, and basic statistical tests; focus on critical interpretation of data as seen in media and politics.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 494: Geometry for Middle School Teachers — proofs, constructions, transformations, visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Review geometric terms and proof techniques (triangle congruence, angle sums), straightedge-and-compass constructions and their correctness, study the four isometries and their compositions, derive area/volume formulas and relationships under dilation, and use The Geometer’s Sketchpad for conjectures and problem solving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course emphasizes visual learning, geoboards, and student research/presentations on enrichment topics; about 50% of instruction uses dynamic geometry software to support conjecture formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 495: Calculus Concepts for Middle School Teachers — intuitive calculus
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce slopes, limits, derivatives, and anti-derivatives using tables, graphs, and real-life examples; derive formulas and apply to optimization and area/volume problems to build intuition rather than formal advanced calculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach via group work and exploratory worksheets; include connections to algebra and graph behavior (higher derivatives and shape).

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 496/596 & MTH 499/599: Problem Solving and Algebraic Problem Solving — strategies and assessment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Master a variety of problem solving strategies (guess and check, tables, diagrams, exhaustive search, logic, pattern recognition, Venn diagrams, algebra) and focus on writing word problems appropriate for middle school and developing scoring rubrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize strategy-to-algebra connections, ratio/percentage/rate/work problems; final projects often include lesson plans and assessment rubrics for classroom use.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 497: Discrete Mathematics for Middle School Teachers — hands-on combinatorics & graph theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce the pigeonhole principle, set theory and inclusion-exclusion, multiplication rule, permutations and combinations, Pascal’s triangle, counting derivations, fractals, and graph theory topics (complete/bipartite graphs, trees, vertex coloring, map coloring) through hands-on activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use attribute pieces, games, and manipulatives to relate discrete math to classroom phenomena (lotteries, games); graduate-level versions emphasize proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ED 434 & ED 436: Content Pedagogy sequence — NCTM principles and curriculum design
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-term sequence focused on teaching process: NCTM Principles (Equity, Curriculum, Teaching, Learning, Assessment, Technology); comparison of national/state standards; designing problem-based lessons, analyzing teacher videos, creating proficiency-based assessments, reflecting on research, and modifying curriculum to raise cognitive demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments center on designing classroom activities, analyzing practice, and aligning instruction/assessment with standards and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundations sequence (MTH 211–213) learning goals
rubrics_metrics.description: MTH 211 covers problem solving, whole number and integer operations, and number theory; MTH 212 focuses on fractions, decimals, probability and statistics; MTH 213 explores geometry — all aimed at deep conceptual understanding and addressing student misconceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses use group work/discovery learning and manipulatives to develop deeper understanding beyond procedural fluency.

rubrics_metrics.name: MTH 396: Elementary Problem Solving — mentoring and creating problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on problem solving techniques, creating word problems for given strategies, and assessing problem solving skills via mentoring local elementary students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical mentoring and writing-assessment experience designed to prepare pre-service teachers to evaluate and support student problem solving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling and accessibility accommodations for pre-service teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: To accommodate students who are student-teaching or working, classes labeled 'for Elementary Teachers' start at 2 P.M. or later and classes 'for Middle School Teachers' start at 5 P.M.; some students may substitute summer courses to satisfy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course scheduling is a programmatic accommodation to enable pre-service teachers to complete coursework around field experiences.
